sources.entry: Neovim - Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/neovim/neovim) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Neovim is a refactored fork of Vim focused on maintainability, extensibility, and letting external UIs and plugins talk to the editor through an API.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Neovim as a project that aggressively refactors Vim to simplify maintenance, split work among developers, enable advanced UIs without changing the core, and maximize extensibility. It lists modern GUIs, API access from many languages (including C/C++, Go, Java/Kotlin, JavaScript/Node.js, Lua, Python, Ruby, Rust and others), an embedded scriptable terminal emulator, asynchronous job control, shared data (shada) across editor instances, XDG base directory support, and compatibility with most Vim plugins. Pre-built packages are offered for Windows, macOS and Linux, and it can be built from source with CMake, wrapped by a Makefile. Contributions after a certain commit are Apache 2.0 licensed, except code copied from Vim.
use_cases: Editing code or text in a Vim-style modal editor
Building a custom editor UI or GUI front end
Scripting the editor from Python, Lua, Ruby or other languages via API
Running an embedded terminal inside the editor
Migrating an existing Vim configuration and plugins
Installing a terminal text editor on Windows, macOS or Linux
notable: Remote API callable from many programming languages
Compatible with most existing Vim plugins
Pre-built packages and distro packages available
caveats: Building from source requires installing dependencies first; see BUILD.md for supported platforms
Vim-copied contributions are not Apache 2.0 licensed, only later contributions are
summary.license: Apache 2.0 for contributions after commit b17d96 (except Vim-copied code); see LICENSE.txt
